title: Movable minors and sevenths
summary: You already own the major E- and A-shape barres. This level adds their minor, 7, m7 and maj7 versions — each one finger away from the shape you know — and the map that makes them useful: every natural note on strings 6 and 5, so any chord name becomes a fret in a second. In My Life and Across the Universe put F♯m, Bm and Gm barres next to open chords, a borrowed iv minor (D → Dm, G → Gm) and the open B7, at slow, exposed tempos where a late barre is easy to hear.
goals: Play major, minor, 7, m7 and maj7 as E-shapes and A-shapes at any fret, from the chord name alone.
Name any note on strings 6 and 5 (frets 0–12) in under two seconds.
Change between barre minors and open chords at 30–40 clean changes a minute.
In My Life and Across the Universe through with the record, no stops.
Play a major key's six chords as barres in A and D, and recognise the borrowed iv when a song uses it.

reading.note: week 1 — the shape families, root on string 6 and 5.
week 1–2 — strings 6 and 5 cold; octave shapes.
week 3 — borrowed iv (Dm in A, Gm in D) and the open B7 as a secondary dominant.
re-read the circle of fifths section, week 4.

song_plan: Core: **Across the Universe** (weeks 1–2 on Song day) and **In My Life** (weeks 3–4); Session D plays both every week. The usual recording of Across the Universe sounds a half step low: tune down a half step to play along, or use the metronome. Swap a core song for an alternate when you can already play it with the record, or when its hard change is still under 15 a minute after two weeks. Alternates, easiest first: *Victoria* (Em → Bm at speed), *Sunday Girl* (barres at frets 2–4, key change), *All My Little Words* (A♭: all barres, or capo 1).

exit_criteria: Benchmark pairs 1–5 at target in two Session Ds in a row.
In My Life with the record, no stops — the D → Dm and the bridge's B7 included.
Across the Universe with the record (or the metronome at 75), no stops.
All 12 notes found on string 6 and then string 5 in 60 seconds or less.
Any chord from the chord-call list played as an E-shape and as an A-shape within three seconds of reading it.
stuck: Not every box ticked after 6 weeks? Move on anyway. Keep one song from this level (a core song or an easier alternate) as a 5-minute play-through in Level 3's Session D, and open every Level 3 Session A primer with your weakest pair until it reaches target.
skip_ahead: Pass every benchmark cold (first attempt, no practice that day) in week 1's Session D? Go straight to Level 3.

drills.title: One-minute changes
drills.instructions: Timer at 1:00. One down-strum per chord, change, strum the other, as fast as you can while staying clean. Count clean landings only. Two rounds per pair; write the better count.

drills.title: Air shapes
drills.instructions: Hand off the neck. Form the barre shape an inch above the strings — index straight, other fingers already curled — land everything at once, strum, check, lift. Ten per shape.

drills.title: Barre pulse
drills.instructions: Hold the barre. Metronome 60: on each click relax to the buzz point, then press until clean. Thumb low and light, pull from the arm. One minute per shape; shake out between.

drills.title: Place and lift
drills.instructions: Fret the shape, relax until the fingers just touch, press again. Twenty presses, one per click at 60, no strumming.

drills.title: Anchor hunt
drills.instructions: Before a new pair, say what stays, what slides along its string, what jumps. Then ten changes keeping anchors down. This level: Bm ↔ F♯m = index stays at fret 2 and rolls flat; Gm7 ↔ C7 = index stays at fret 3, ring moves one string; Em7 ↔ Gm = the top-string G stays (little finger hands it to the index).

drills.title: Change loop
drills.instructions: Strum chord 1 once, change, strum chord 2 once, stop, reset. Ten clean in a row; a miss sets the count back to zero.

drills.title: Tempo ladder
drills.instructions: One chord per bar, four down-strums. Start where the change is perfect (try 50). Three clean passes: +4 bpm. A miss: −8 bpm. Write the top clean tempo in today's blank.

drills.title: Leave early
drills.instructions: Down-up eighths. On the last “and” before a barre, let go and strum open strings while travelling. Use it into every barre in both core songs.

drills.title: Eyes closed
drills.instructions: Make the change without looking; open your eyes after landing to check. Ten times.

drills.title: Song loop
drills.instructions: Loop the two bars around the hard change in the song's own rhythm, 10 bpm under this week's tempo. Then add a bar either side. Then the whole section.

drills.title: Random pairs
drills.instructions: Write the 15 chord names from the chord page on scraps, plus Em. Draw two, do one-minute changes, write the pair and count on the back of the sheet. Draw again.

drills.title: Shape-family walk
drills.instructions: One bar each, metronome 60 → 80, barre never lifts. **E-shape at fret 3:** G 355433 → Gm 355333 (lift middle) → G7 353433 (lift little finger) → Gm7 353333. **A-shape at fret 3:** C x35553 → Cm x35543 → C7 x35353 → Cm7 x35343. Then the same walks at E-shape fret 5 (A) and 7 (B), A-shape fret 5 (D) and 2 (B).

drills.title: Root finding on strings 6 and 5
drills.instructions: Notes in this order: **F B♭ D A♭ C♯ G E♭ B F♯ C A E**. Say each, play it on string 6 (frets 0–12), next. Then the same list on string 5. Timer running; write the seconds. Landmarks: string 6 — G 3, A 5, C 8, E 12; string 5 — C 3, D 5, F 8, A 12.

drills.title: Chord call
drills.instructions: Read a chord from this list, find its root on string 6, play it as an E-shape; find the root on string 5, play it as an A-shape. **B♭m, E♭7, F♯m7, Cm, D7, G♯m, A7, Fm7, B7, C♯m, Gm7, E♭m, Bmaj7, Am7.** Start where you left off last time.

drills.title: Octave shapes
drills.instructions: Root on string 6 → same note on string 4, two frets higher. Root on string 5 → string 3, two frets higher. Play each note of the root-finding list as an octave pair, saying the name.

drills.title: Scale in 3rds
drills.instructions: In this week's position play pairs a 3rd apart (1–3, 2–4, 3–5 …) to the top and back down. Quarters at 60 until clean, then eighths.

drills.title: Scale, then its chords
drills.instructions: Scale up and down once, then the key's chords as barres, one bar each, saying the numbers. **A:** A (E5) Bm (A2) C♯m (A4) D (A5) E (A7) F♯m (E2) = I ii iii IV V vi. **D:** D (A5) Em (E7, or open) F♯m (E2) G (E3) A (E5) Bm (A2). Then I–vi–IV–V and I–IV–iv–I (the borrowed iv: Dm in A, Gm in D).

drills.title: Make something
drills.instructions: Pick a key (A or D). Use four chords: I, one minor (ii, iii or vi) as a barre, one 7 or m7, and the borrowed iv minor. Loop four beats each; each pass change one thing — order, a 7th, a different shape for the same chord, or the rhythm. Write the keeper in Notes.

sessions.name: A
sessions.title: Chord day
sessions.focus: Barre families and this week's three pairs (week plan, column 1). Pair 1 is the hard one.

blocks.title: Primer: today's shapes
blocks.instructions: Barre pulse on Gm (E3) and Cm (A3), one minute each. Then air shapes ×10 on both chords of pair 1. Carried a weak pair from Level 1? Change-loop it for the last minute.

blocks.title: Pair 1: the full recipe
blocks.instructions: Anchor hunt (say what stays, slides, jumps) → slow motion ×5 → change loop to 10 clean → tempo ladder from 50, one chord per bar. Stop at the clock.

blocks.title: Pairs 2 and 3
blocks.instructions: Change loop to 10 clean on each, then one-minute changes: two rounds each. Write the better count. (Week 1: pairs 2 and 3 are walks — loop each for a minute and count clean changes.)

blocks.title: Shape-family walk
blocks.instructions: E-shape walk at fret 3, then fret 5; A-shape walk at fret 3, then fret 5. Barre never lifts.

blocks.title: Fretboard: chord call
blocks.instructions: Five chords from the chord-call list, each as an E-shape and an A-shape. Say the root's fret aloud before you play it.

blocks.title: Song: put pair 1 back in
blocks.instructions: In this week's song section: song loop on the two bars with pair 1, then the section ×2 at this week's tempo, leaving early into every barre.

blocks.title: Log
blocks.instructions: Log page: tick A, write the minutes. In Notes: the change that felt worst today.

sessions.name: B
sessions.title: Fretboard day
sessions.focus: Notes on strings 6 and 5, one movable scale position, and chords as numbers in a key (week plan, column 2).

blocks.title: Primer
blocks.instructions: Air shapes ×10 on the two chords of pair 1, then the change with eyes closed ×10.

blocks.title: Notes on the strings
blocks.instructions: Week 1: string 6. Week 2: string 5. Week 3: octave shapes. Week 4: both strings, against the clock. Root-finding list, twice; time the second run.

blocks.title: This week's scale
blocks.instructions: The E-shape position (diagram at G, fret 3; week 2 at A, fret 5; week 4 at D, fret 10). Say the root at every square. Quarters at 60, then eighths on the tempo ladder. Week 3: in 3rds.

blocks.title: Scale, then its chords
blocks.instructions: Weeks 1–3 in A, week 4 in D: the six chords as barres with numbers, then I–vi–IV–V and I–IV–iv–I. Name each root's fret before you move.

blocks.title: Song by numbers: In My Life
blocks.instructions: Verse = I V | vi I7 | IV iv | I (A E | F♯m A7 | D Dm | A). Play it ×4 at this week's IML tempo. Then the same numbers in G with barres: G D | Em G7 | C Cm | G.

blocks.title: Log
blocks.instructions: Log page: tick B, write the minutes. Notes: the notes on strings 6/5 that are still slow.

sessions.name: C
sessions.title: Song day
sessions.focus: Longest song block: isolate this week's hard change (pair 1), then play the section and the song in time. Weeks 1–2 Across the Universe, weeks 3–4 In My Life.

blocks.title: Primer
blocks.instructions: Barre pulse (1 min) on the barre chord in pair 1, then place-and-lift ×20 and air shapes ×10 on both chords.

blocks.title: The hard change
blocks.instructions: Change loop to 10 clean, then tempo ladder one chord per bar from 50.

blocks.title: Fretboard: roots first
blocks.instructions: Read this week's section. For every chord, say its root and play that note on string 6 or 5 in time, one per bar — the bass line of the song.

blocks.title: This week's song
blocks.instructions: Song loop round the hard change (5 min). The week's section ×3 at this week's tempo. Then the whole form without stopping — fumble through. Weeks 3–4: the last 5 minutes with the record.

blocks.title: The other core song
blocks.instructions: Once through at this week's tempo for it, leaving early into every barre. Mark any bar that broke.

blocks.title: Log
blocks.instructions: Log page: tick C, write the minutes. Notes: the bar where you stopped, if any.

sessions.name: D
sessions.title: Mix and measure
sessions.focus: Short versions of everything, the benchmarks with numbers, one Level 1 review, and five minutes of your own music.

blocks.title: Primer
blocks.instructions: Air shapes ×5 on every chord in benchmarks 1–5. The tests are taken cold.

blocks.title: Benchmarks
blocks.instructions: One-minute changes, one round each: **1** Bm ↔ F♯m · **2** Em7 ↔ Gm · **3** F♯m ↔ A7 · **4** B7 ↔ Dm · **5** Gm7 ↔ C7. Root finding, timed. A major position (fret 5) in eighths, tempo ladder from 70. Write all seven numbers in the log.

blocks.title: Review from Level 1
blocks.instructions: One-minute changes on Emaj7/G♯ (466450) ↔ Em/G (322000) — or the pair you carried from Level 1. Then the Reckoner bridge once with the record (chart in the Level 1 packet).

blocks.title: Songs, measured
blocks.instructions: In My Life, then Across the Universe — with the record from week 3, at this week's tempo before that. Write benchmarks 8 and 9 in the log.

blocks.title: Make something
blocks.instructions: Key of A or D: I, a barre minor, a 7 or m7, and the borrowed iv. Loop, change one thing per pass, write the keeper in Notes.

blocks.title: Log and exit check
blocks.instructions: Tick D in the log. Tick any exit box you passed today. Week 6 or all boxes ticked? Fill in the check-in sheet.
